title.narrative: JP Driving Climate Resilience and Nature-Positive Growth

description.narrative: The Joint Programme (JP) for Ghana, across both phases, aims to catalyze the transition to sustainable, resilient, and equitable food systems through innovative financing and nature-positive soybean value chain development. The JP will pilot and scale climate-smart production, circular processing, nutrition-sensitive procurement, and policy alignment—enabling 10,000+ youth and women to engage in green agribusiness, improving dietary diversity for 1 million+ schoolchildren, and restoring 10,000+ hectares of degraded land. Expected yield increases of 40%, food loss reduction by 50%, and boosted processor capacity (30%) will strengthen food and income security. Under the programme, UNDP will explore the possibility of introducing a Loan Portfolio Guarantee Facility to de-risk private sector lending, enabling inclusive finance for farmers and MSMEs. Well also look at setting up a national Platform to harmonize policies and subsidies with climate and biodiversity commitments, fostering an enabling environment for sustained transformation.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
